finding.capture: Traffic is being saved to disk.
finding.readOnly: Settings are read-only in this mode.

guards.title: Cloud guards
guards.note: Turning a guard off asks first, and saving asks for your password. The guards act only while proxy mode is on.

toggle.inactive: Inactive while the proxy is off.

proxy_mode.label: Proxy to PetKit's cloud
proxy_mode.description: Forwards every device request to the real PetKit cloud and answers with its reply. Only for adding a model nobody has captured yet.

proxy_block_run_cmd.label: Block remote shell commands
proxy_block_run_cmd.description: Strips shell commands the cloud tries to run on the device.
proxy_block_run_cmd.offWarning: While the proxy is on, the real PetKit cloud could run shell commands on your device as root.

proxy_block_ota.label: Block firmware updates
proxy_block_ota.description: Answers the OTA endpoints locally and drops firmware images found anywhere else.
proxy_block_ota.offWarning: While the proxy is on, the real PetKit cloud could push a firmware image to your device.

proxy_block_log_upload.label: Block log uploads
proxy_block_log_upload.description: Withholds the token the device needs to send its debug log to PetKit.
proxy_block_log_upload.offWarning: While the proxy is on, your device could send its debug log to PetKit.

proxy_mqtt_bridge.label: Upstream MQTT bridge
proxy_mqtt_bridge.description: Also bridges the device's MQTT session to the real Aliyun broker.

proxy_media_real_oss.label: Media to the real OSS
proxy_media_real_oss.description: Lets the device upload recordings to PetKit instead of this server. Nothing lands locally.

proxy_local_cvr_window.label: Keep recording locally
proxy_local_cvr_window.description: Ignores the cloud's subscription window and tells the camera its storage is active. A lapsed PetKit plan otherwise stops recording with no error anywhere.

capture.label: Save traffic
capture.description: Records every HTTP request and MQTT message to JSONL files, signing secrets included. Read them under Capture.

problem.dns: The upstream resolver must be an IPv4 address, optionally with a port.
problem.upstream: The upstream host must be a preset or an http(s) URL.

save.unsaved_one: {{count}} unsaved change: <keys>{{keys}}</keys>. Saving asks for your password.
save.unsaved_other: {{count}} unsaved changes: <keys>{{keys}}</keys>. Saving asks for your password.

upstream.none: No calls forwarded yet. A device polls about every 10 seconds.
upstream.refusedNote: The cloud refuses every session-bearing call. That is expected once this server has taken the device over, since the session it presents is one we issued; the device is served our own answers throughout.
upstream.hostNote: A PetKit or Aliyun IoT URL. Every device request is forwarded there with its credential.
upstream.resolverNote: Only used to find the server above. Leave empty unless your router or Pi-hole points PetKit's names at this server: then it would point them here for us too, and the proxy would reach itself instead of the cloud.

retention.title: Keep
retention.description: Over the size cap the oldest files go first; past the age cap they go regardless of size. The sweep runs about every 10 minutes. Leave a field blank for no cap: 0 also means no cap, not "delete everything". Blocked attempts are tiny and rare, so a long window costs almost nothing.

blocked.title: Blocked attempts
blocked.intro: What the cloud tried to do and was stopped. Kept in the database, so the list outlives a restart. Payloads can hold a real device secret, so they are masked; revealing them asks for your password.
blocked.loadFailed: Blocked attempts could not be loaded. {{error}}

connection.title: Connection
connection.intro: Bound at startup. Change these in the server configuration, then restart.

version.label: Version
version.note: The code actually running. If an update did not take effect this still shows the old number, the quickest way to tell a stale build from a real bug.

apiUrl.label: API URL
apiUrl.note: The URL a device calls. Most models take it over Bluetooth from Provision; the oldest, which have no Bluetooth setup, need a DNS redirect.

mqttHost.label: MQTT host
mqttHost.note: Every device is handed this server’s own broker, derived from the API URL host. A patched device connects over MQTT; an unpatched one keeps to the HTTP heartbeat, and commands fall back to it.

mqttPort.label: MQTT broker port
mqttPort.note: The plain port, and the TLS port when TLS is on.

cert.label: TLS certificate
cert.note: The self-signed certificate the broker presents. Missing means the file named by cert_path is not there, and a device that expects TLS will not connect.

auth.label: MQTT auth
auth.note: Accept-all is fine on a trusted LAN; strict enforces the Aliyun HMAC-SHA256 sign.

bridge.label: Bridge to Home Assistant
bridge.note: The connection to Home Assistant’s broker, not the one devices talk to: a device can be healthy while this is down. Disabled means publishing was switched off, a valid way to run.
